title: Zendesk: customer ticket management and response from Teams
availability: AI teammate: Frontier-program access required by the source
overview: Microsoft describes service engineers viewing and managing a customer's Zendesk tickets inside Teams, then communicating with customers and internal teams without switching applications.
published_facts: The integration surfaces all tickets for a customer in context within Teams.
Service engineers can communicate with customers and internal teams from Microsoft 365.
Agent activity is described as visible through Agent 365 observability.

sources.title: Ecosystem partner agents available in Agent 365 - Zendesk
sources.verification: Primary page and Zendesk section fetched and read directly.

a365_relationship: Direct: the Zendesk integration is explicitly listed under Agent 365; no specific customer deployment is asserted.
intent: Find a customer's support tickets in Teams, review the relevant ticket context and send an appropriate response.
actors: Service engineer, Zendesk agent, customer and internal support team; one Agent role abstracts the tool workflow.
published_outcome: Documented in-context ticket management and communication, not a verified resolution rate.

actions.description: Find the customer's Zendesk tickets in context.
Review and manage the relevant ticket context.
Prepare a response using that ticket context.
Communicate the response to the selected customer or internal team.

local_assumptions: Preparing a response is an explicit modeling step within the source's communication workflow; no Zendesk internal implementation is claimed.
A local test contract distinguishes a sent response from one merely queued.
Independent response approval and exact destination allowlisting are local test controls; the source does not mandate them.
limitations: The model cannot determine whether the reply actually solves the customer's problem.
Customer identity, ticket access and tenant entitlement require real authenticated integrations.
Refunds and customer-credit issuance are not modeled because the source does not describe those actions.
